newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban battle opposition north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Taleban battle opposition north of Kabul.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia attacked opposition forces northeast of the town of Jabal-os-Siraj on Saturday, taking two villages, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said five fighters from both sides were killed and 12 wounded in the clashes near Jabal-os-Siraj, which straddles the main road linking Kabul to northern Afghanistan.

AIP said the fighting followed an attack launched on Friday by opposition forces led by former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood near the town of Charikar, 20 km (13 miles) south of Jabal-os-Siraj.
Four Taleban were killed in that clash, it said.

The Taleban, who captured the Afghan capital Kabul in September, are trying to impose their strict Islamic rule across the whole of the central Asian country, of which they already control two-thirds.
In Kabul on Friday night, an opposition warplane dropped a bomb on the airport, hitting a building occupied by Taleban combatants, airport sources said.
"An unknown number of Taleban were killed or wounded," one source at the airport said on Saturday.
Red tracers from anti-aircraft fire crisscrossed the sky as Taleban gunners took aim at the solo jet.
